waterbody.nameAsReported: Incarizan River (also called Geladioc River in EMB reports)
waterbody.habitatScope: River connected to Sorsogon Bay and Ticao Pass; the thesis distinguishes upstream, midstream and downstream zones and reports estuarine/marine-affinity taxa downstream.
waterbody.geometryStatus: No authoritative river boundary, station coordinates or per-taxon location geometry recovered. The municipal profile is locality context only.

thesisIdentity.titleAsReported: Diversity and Abundance of Fish in Incarizan River
thesisIdentity.authentication: The 62-page copy is hosted by a third party. No official SorSU catalog accession, repository record, original file, author upload or confirmation from the university was located. SorSU's official history says its university declaration ceremony was held in 2021; the copy's AY 2019-2020 title-page institutional label therefore needs metadata verification. This discrepancy alone does not establish authenticity or inauthenticity.
thesisIdentity.rights: Scribd displays All Rights Reserved. No item-specific thesis reuse permission or open license was located. No raw copy retained; do not reproduce thesis text, figures or table content in the app.

methodsAndScope.reportedApproach: The thesis describes direct capture with multiple hook-and-line, gill nets and hook-and-line, plus fish obtained indirectly from local fishers; specimens were reportedly examined using morphometric and meristic characters.
methodsAndScope.reportedStations: Methods identify seven stations from Pili through Tula-Tula, Santa Elena, Incarizan and Bacalon to Sitio Tinago and Banacud. The abstract says six sites. The station map and station-level taxa crosswalk could not be validated from the extracted text.
methodsAndScope.samplingDates: No exact field collection dates or seasons were identified; AY 2019-2020 is not a sampling date.
methodsAndScope.voucherAndCoordinates: No specimen accession numbers, museum/depository crosswalk, event-level coordinates, uncertainty, per-taxon station matrix, or direct-versus-fisher-sourced taxon flags were identified in the reviewed text.
methodsAndScope.habitatInterpretation: Do not treat the reported downstream assemblage as exclusively freshwater: the paper describes a connected estuarine river and identifies brackish/marine/reef-associated taxa in downstream sections.

claimsAsReported.interpretation: This is a transcription of source claims for internal research triage only, not a verified occurrence dataset. Names are preserved as shown; no silent taxonomic repair or freshwater/native/status assignment was made.

qualityFlags.issue: The abstract says six study sites; the methods and results describe seven.
qualityFlags.decision: Retain both statements and seek the original thesis or author clarification.

qualityFlags.issue: The thesis claims 715 individuals, 26 genera and 21 families, but extracted taxonomy rows include three genus-only entries and apparent spelling/format errors. The abstract's family list also repeats some families.
qualityFlags.decision: Do not interpret the table as 26 confirmed species or an app-ready checklist.

qualityFlags.issue: Examples requiring source-image and taxonomic checks include Glossogobius guiris, Ostorhincus fasciatus, Leionathus daura, and varying spellings of Ambassis gymnocephalus, Hyporhamphus limbatus, Scorpaena plumieri and Epinephelus sexfasciatus in narrative text.
qualityFlags.decision: Preserve verbatim spellings; verify each against a dated taxonomic authority and original specimen/document before normalizing.

qualityFlags.issue: Direct gear catches and fisher-provided specimens are combined without a taxon-by-method crosswalk; no vouchers or coordinates are stated in the reviewed text.
qualityFlags.decision: Do not promote source rows to georeferenced occurrence events or independently collected specimens.

qualityFlags.issue: The source is historical and the river connects to Sorsogon Bay; taxa may reflect freshwater, brackish, estuarine or marine-connected reaches.
qualityFlags.decision: Keep habitat/reach distinctions; infer neither current presence nor a strictly freshwater inventory.

administrativeContext.locality: The Municipality of Magallanes' 2017 profile names Incarizan among natural tributaries draining toward Ticao Pass and Sorsogon Bay. It provides no official river geometry or taxon data.
classificationConflict: EMB Region V's 2019 report says Geladioc (Incarizan) River conforms to Class C.
EMB Region V's 2022 report table lists Geladioc River (Incarizan River) as Class C, year 2022.
EMB Region V's 2024 report table lists the same river as Class B, classified/reclassified in 2019 under DMC No. 2022-15.
administrativeContext.decision: The controlling DENR circular was not independently retrieved and the official annual-report entries conflict. Do not publish a current water class, legal-use, water-quality or fishing-safety statement from this material.

nextAction: Ask SorSU-Magallanes Campus Library or the authors for the catalog record/original thesis and confirm exact study dates, stations, table spellings, specimen repository, identification basis and reuse conditions. Meanwhile continue with distinct Sorsogon coastal/market evidence without mapping market records to Incarizan River. Seek the controlling DMC No. 2022-15 before any water-class display.
